abstract: First introns of mammalian genes are often longer than other introns and may contain regulatory elements, suggesting that they may have roles in gene regulation. We detected a previously unannotated, low abundance intronic transcript, TP53-INT1, using long-read direct RNA sequencing data. TP53-INT1 has low coding potential and terminates within the first and longest intron of TP53. The transcript structure and 3'-end were validated by independent experimental and in silico evidence. We identified a canonical polyadenylation signal upstream of the transcript termination site and demonstrated its functionality using reporter assays. Furthermore, a potential G-quadruplex (G4)-forming sequence was identified upstream of this polyadenylation signal. The G4-forming potential was confirmed using spectroscopic and thermal stability analyses. Complementing the in vitro characterizations, treatment with Pyridostatin, a G4-stabilizing drug, was associated with decreased TP53 expression. Together, these findings characterize a previously unannotated TP53 intronic transcript and reveal a local genomic context combining accessible chromatin, a functional polyadenylation signal, and a potential G4-forming sequence that may influence full-length transcription.
